items.title: Drupal core - Highly critical - Access bypass - SA-CORE-2026-019
items.summary:
Project: 
Drupal core
Project machine name: 
drupal
Date: 
2026-November-25
Security risk: 
Highly critical 21 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:None/CI:All/II:All/E:Exploit/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Access bypass
Affected versions: 
<10.6.23 || >= 11.0.0 <11.3.23 || >=11.4.0 <11.4.14
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-136716
Description: 

Drupal core ships with an install.php file for installing Drupal core.

If you have already secured the installer, you are not vulnerable.

SA-CORE-2026-017 recently fixed several vulnerabilities within the Drupal core installer. However, certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain vulnerable to site takeover following that advisory, including production sites. It is not apparent in the user interface if a site is in the affected vulnerable state, and sites that are already compromised may no longer be in the vulnerable state.

This is being exploited in the wild. Any site that left its installer remotely accessible following SA-CORE-2026-017 may still have been compromised.

  • Check your site logs for unauthorized access, especially unexpected changes to or by the user 1 account.

  • Ensure the user 1 email address is set to something you control, and consider resetting user 1's password.

  • If it appears your site may have been compromised based on the above, review Your Drupal site got hacked. Now what?.

Drupal Steward information:

This issue and SA-CORE-2026-017 are both being protected by Drupal Steward. Sites and platforms that use Drupal Steward's recommended mitigations are already protected from known attack vectors, but sites should upgrade in the near future in case additional attack vectors are discovered.

Solution: 

  1. Install the latest version:

    Drupal 11

    • If you use Drupal 11.4.x, update to Drupal 11.4.14.
    • If you use Drupal 11.3.x, update to Drupal 11.3.23.
    • Drupal 11.2.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

    Drupal 10

    • If you use Drupal 10.6.x, update to Drupal 10.6.23.
    • Drupal 10.5.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

  2. Run update.php. An update hook must run to fix existing production sites in this state.

  3. Strongly recommended: Follow the instructions for securing the Drupal installer on all new and existing sites.

Drupal 8 and Drupal 9 have both reached end-of-life.

items.title: Drupal core - Moderately critical - Gadget chain - SA-CORE-2026-018
items.summary:
Project: 
Drupal core
Project machine name: 
drupal
Date: 
2026-November-18
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 14 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:Admin/CI:All/II:All/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Gadget chain
Affected versions: 
<10.6.22 || >=11.0.0 <11.3.22 || >=11.4.0 <11.4.13
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-132166
Description: 

Drupal core contains a chain of methods that could be exploitable when an insecure deserialization vulnerability exists on the site. This so-called "gadget chain" presents no direct threat, but is a vector that can be used to achieve remote code execution if the application deserializes untrusted data due to another vulnerability.

This issue is not directly exploitable.

This issue is mitigated by the fact that in order for it to be exploitable, a separate vulnerability must be present to allow an attacker to pass unsafe input to unserialize().

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

Drupal 11

  • If you use Drupal 11.4.x, update to Drupal 11.4.13.
  • If you use Drupal 11.3.x, update to Drupal 11.3.22.
  • Drupal 11.2.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

Drupal 10

  • If you use Drupal 10.6.x, update to Drupal 10.6.22.
  • Drupal 10.5.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

Drupal 8 and Drupal 9 have both reached end-of-life.

Affected versions: 
<10.6.22 || >=11.0.0 <11.3.22 || >=11.4.0 <11.4.13
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-132165
Description: 

Update: the Security Team has received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC.

Drupal core ships with an install.php file for installing Drupal core.

Under specific conditions, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal. This can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution.

Some (but not all) exploit paths are mitigated if the web server cannot write to or change permissions on settings.php. In addition to upgrading, the Drupal Security Team recommends securing the Drupal installer after installation.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-GMRPK0BU.

Drupal Steward protection:

This issue is being protected by Drupal Steward. Sites that use Drupal Steward are already protected from known attack vectors, but sites should upgrade in the near future in case additional attack vectors are discovered.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

Drupal 11

  • If you use Drupal 11.4.x, update to Drupal 11.4.13.
  • If you use Drupal 11.3.x, update to Drupal 11.3.22.
  • Drupal 11.2.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

Drupal 10

  • If you use Drupal 10.6.x, update to Drupal 10.6.22.
  • Drupal 10.5.x and below are end-of-life and do not receive security coverage.

Drupal 8 and Drupal 9 have both reached end-of-life.

If you cannot upgrade immediately:

Follow the instructions for securing the Drupal installer to protect your site from attacks.

items.title: Upcoming critical Drupal core releases on November 18, 2026 - PSA-2026-11-16
items.summary:
Date: 
2026-November-16
Security risk: 
Critical 18 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:None/CI:All/II:All/E:Proof/TD:Uncommon
Description: 

There will be a Drupal core security release for all supported branches on November 18, 2026 between 17:00 and 21:00 UTC. (To see this in your local timezone, refer to the Drupal Core Calendar.)

The Drupal Security Team urges you to reserve time for core updates at that time because exploits might be developed within hours or days.

The vulnerabilities are currently rated as critical and at least one can be exploited by anonymous users. More than one configuration is affected, so do not assume your site is safe.

We also recommend updating to the latest supported patch (bugfix) release for your site's version of Drupal before November 18, so that you can address any other upgrade issues before the security window.

Drupal Steward information

This issue is being mitigated by Drupal Steward. Sites that use Drupal Steward are already protected from known attack vectors. Other security advisories may be released on the same date without Drupal Steward mitigation. Sites should upgrade in the near future to ensure that they are protected from all published advisories.

Affected versions

All currently supported versions of Drupal core are affected, including:

  • Drupal 11.4.x
  • Drupal 11.3.x
  • Drupal 10.6.x

Drupal 12.0.0-beta3 and 11.5.0-beta1 are also affected. New beta or release candidate versions will be provided following the security updates for the currently supported branches.

All versions of Drupal prior to 10.6.x as well as all versions of Drupal 11 prior to 11.3.x are end-of-life and no longer supported. Sites on those versions should apply the interim mitigation steps that will be provided in the upcoming security advisory, and update as soon as possible to avoid this and other publicly disclosed vulnerabilities.

Disclosure policy

Neither the Security Team nor any other party is able to release any more information about this vulnerability until the announcement is made. Security release announcements will appear on the Drupal.org security advisory page, which has RSS feeds. The announcement will also be made public on:

  • The #security-team channel of the Drupal community Slack
  • Bluesky
  • Mastodon
  • X (formerly Twitter)
  • LinkedIn
  • By email for those who have subscribed to our email list. (To subscribe to the email list: log in on Drupal.org, go to your user profile page and subscribe to the security newsletter on the Edit » My newsletters tab.)

If you have received an unsolicited email describing a potential Drupal core security issue, please do not forward it or act on instructions in it.

items.title: Data field - Moderately critical - Cross-site scripting - SA-CONTRIB-2026-339
items.summary:
Project: 
Data field
Project machine name: 
datafield
Date: 
2026-November-11
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 12 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:User/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:Uncommon
Vulnerability: 
Cross-site scripting
Affected versions: 
<2.0.15 || >=3.0.0 <3.0.1
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126760
Description: 

This module provides a field type for storing structured data with multiple sub-fields, along with several widgets including a Search - autocomplete widget.

The module’s autocomplete endpoint does not sufficiently escape stored field values before returning them as suggestion labels, which can allow cross-site scripting.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that the attacker must have permission to edit an entity carrying a Data Field field. The Search - autocomplete widget must also be configured on that field.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use Data Field 3.0.x, upgrade to Data Field 3.0.1.
  • If you use Data Field 2.0.x, upgrade to Data Field 2.0.15.

items.title: File Resumable Upload - Moderately critical - Improper authorization - SA-CONTRIB-2026-338
items.summary:
Project: 
File Resumable Upload
Project machine name: 
file_resup
Date: 
2026-November-11
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 13 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:None/CI:None/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Improper authorization
Affected versions: 
<2.0.6
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126747
Description: 

This module adds large file, multiple file, and resumable uploads to the File and Image field widgets.

The module doesn't sufficiently check access to resumable upload forms. This allows an unauthenticated user to start uploads against forms they are not permitted to use, and to store partial upload data on the server.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that partial upload data is only attached to content through the normal entity form, which enforces its own access checks, and that stored partial upload data is not executable by the web server.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to File Resumable Upload 2.0.6.

CVE-2026-126746
Description: 

The S3 File System CORS Upload module lets users upload files straight from the browser to Amazon S3 (or an S3-compatible service), using a file widget on entity forms.

The module doesn't sufficiently restrict the upload permission it gives the browser. A user who can upload through the widget can overwrite other files already stored in the bucket, including files they couldn't otherwise replace.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must have access to a form that uses the S3 File System CORS Upload widget.

Solution:

  • Upgrade to S3 File System CORS Upload 8.x-1.4.

Moderately critical 10 ∕ 25 AC:Basic/A:User/CI:Some/II:None/E:Theoretical/TD:Default
Vulnerability: 
Twig injection
Affected versions: 
<2.0.1
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126745
Description: 

This module enables you to display users by a configurable "real name" pattern built from tokens, instead of by their username.

The module does not sufficiently sanitize user input used in name patterns.
A user can place Twig syntax in their own profile data and have it evaluated when their name is displayed.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that the site must be configured with a real name pattern that includes user-supplied data, and the attacker must be able to edit that data on their own account.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to Real Name 2.0.1.

Existing stored real names are cleared on update so that they will be regenerated by the corrected code.

items.title: Layout Builder iFrame Modal - Moderately critical - Cross-site scripting - SA-CONTRIB-2026-335
items.summary:
Project: 
Layout Builder iFrame Modal
Project machine name: 
layout_builder_iframe_modal
Date: 
2026-November-11
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 13 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:User/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Cross-site scripting
Affected versions: 
<1.3.9
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126744
Description: 

This module renders Layout Builder forms inside an iframe in a modal dialog, using the admin theme.

The module provides its own Ajax command to open the iframe dialog. This command does not sanitize the dialog options the same way Drupal core does since SA-CORE-2026-001, which can lead to a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must be able to control the Ajax response, or be able to add markup with specific attributes to a page.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to Layout Builder iFrame Modal 1.3.9.

The fix relies on the dialog option sanitization added to Drupal core in SA-CORE-2026-001. Make sure the site also runs a Drupal core version that includes that fix (10.5.9, 10.6.7, 11.2.11, 11.3.7 or later).

items.title: COOKiES Consent Management - Moderately critical - Cross-site scripting - SA-CONTRIB-2026-334
items.summary:
Project:

Project machine name:

2026-November-11
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 12 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:Admin/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:All
Vulnerability: 
Cross-site scripting
Affected versions: 
<1.2.17
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126743
Description: 

This module enables you to manage user consent for external services, such as embedded videos. The COOKiES Video submodule blocks external video elements until the visitor accepts the consent banner, then re-enables them.

The module doesn't sufficiently check the value of the data-cookies-video-blazy-src attribute when it converts it back to a src attribute for Blazy iframes. The protocol check added in SA-CONTRIB-2025-092 covered the other conversion paths but missed this one.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must have the correct permissions to have a specific HTML element display for all users, and that element must have a specific class set.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use version 1.2.x, upgrade to COOKiES Consent Management 1.2.17.

This module implements a field formatter for text fields that improves the Summary or Trimmed formatter built into Drupal core.

The module doesn't sufficiently escape unsafe HTML when passed through the module's Twig filter.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must have a role with the ability to post content that gets passed through a Twig template with one of the |smart_trim_* filters provided by this module.

If a site uses only use the field formatter without the Twig filter, it is not vulnerable.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use version 2.2.x, upgrade to Smart Trim 2.2.2.

This module tracks file downloads for private files and provides reports about them.

The module provides the permissions that are never actually checked. A user with only the View download counts permission could export the download log and delete all download records.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must have an account with the View download counts permission.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • If you use Download Count 2.x, upgrade to Download Count 3.0.2.
  • If you use Download Count 2.x, upgrade to Download Count 2.2.5.

After the update, grant the permissions reset download counts and export download counts only to the roles that need them.

Description: 

This module enables you to create custom pages and to override existing paths, such as node or user pages, with variants that are selected by conditions.

The Page Manager UI submodule doesn't sufficiently protect against cross-site request forgery (CSRF). An attacker could trick a user with permission to administer pages into enabling or disabling a page without their knowledge.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that the Page Manager UI submodule must be enabled, and the targeted user must have the "administer pages" permission.

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to Page Manager 8.x-4.1.

After updating, run database updates (or clear caches) so the change takes effect.

As a workaround, uninstall the Page Manager UI submodule on production sites. Pages that already exist keep working without it.

items.title: Entity Print - Moderately critical - Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data - SA-CONTRIB-2026-327
items.summary:
Project: 
Entity Print
Project machine name: 
entity_print
Date: 
2026-November-11
Security risk: 
Moderately critical 12 ∕ 25 AC:Complex/A:User/CI:Some/II:Some/E:Theoretical/TD:Default
Vulnerability: 
Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data
Affected versions: 
<2.20.0
CVE IDs: 
CVE-2026-126736
Description: 

This module enables you to print and export Drupal entities to PDF and other formats, using print engines such as Dompdf.

When generating a PDF for a page that contains third-party resources, the module sends several kinds of private data to the third-party server (including the user's session cookie and their Dompdf HTTP authentication credentials), regardless of the host those resources are loaded from. A third-party site referenced in printed content can therefore obtain the session data of users printing that content and use it to impersonate them.

This vulnerability is mitigated by the fact that to deliberately exploit this vulnerability, an attacker must be able to create or edit content using a text format that allows images or stylesheets from arbitrary sites (such as "Full HTML").

Solution: 

Install the latest version:

  • Upgrade to Entity Print 8.x-2.20.

Sites unable to upgrade immediately can disable the Enable Remote URLs setting of the Dompdf print engine to mitigate the vulnerability.
